messages.subject: 0 being substituted for NA in cast
messages.subject_clean: 0 being substituted for NA in cast
messages.body_plain:
Dear list,

I have come across some odd (to me) behaviour, which may or may not be as desired/expected.

I find that cast occasionally substitutes NA for 0. Note, this is not for 'structural missingness' (as I read about in the earlier post here <https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#%21searchin/manipulatr/0$20NA$20substitute/manipulatr/jVbuHuq7sjA/kco4xoT_q-MJ>), but where NA is the result of a function evaluation.

I can fix the problem by adding fill = NA to the cast arguments, however, I'd still be interested to know if this behaviour is expected or not.

The manner in which this happens doesn't appear consistent. Example below to illustrate what I mean. I've had to reproduce the weird application of cast I was using when I ran into the problem to reproduce the error.

library(reshape)

# Some functions
len2  <- function(x) sum(!is.na <http://is.na>(x))

sem   <- function(x, valid = 100) if(len2(x) >= valid)
                                    sd(x, na.rm=TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na <http://is.na>(x))) else NA

mean2 <- function(x, valid = 100) if(len2(x) >= valid)
                                    mean(x, na.rm=TRUE) else NA

# Generate one data set (test.df1)
set.seed(454)
# Around half the categories will have 99 values, and so
# their summary statistic functions should return NA
ctgry    <- factor(rep(LETTERS[1:10], round(runif(10, 99,100))))
# Add a value field to aggregate
test.df1 <- data.frame(ctgry, value   = rnorm(length(ctgry)))

# Generate another equivalent, but slightly different one (test.df2)
set.seed(1)
# Around half the categories will have 99 values, and so
# their summary statistic functions should return NA
ctgry    <- factor(rep(LETTERS[1:10], round(runif(10, 99,100))))
# Add a value field to aggregate
test.df2 <- data.frame(ctgry, value   = rnorm(length(ctgry)))

# All rows with 99 responses should have NA for mean2 and sem!

# Here, occasionally values which should be NA, are 0
cast(test.df1, ctgry ~., c(mean2, sem, len2))
# Rows 2, 3, 6, and 8 report 0s. 1 and 4 report 2 NAs as expected

###      ctgry       mean2        sem len2
###   1      A          NA         NA   99
###   2      B  0.00000000         NA   99
###   3      C          NA 0.00000000   99
###   4      D          NA         NA   99
###   5      E  0.06946066 0.09761598  100
###   6      F  0.00000000         NA   99
###   7      G -0.12603771 0.09988778  100
###   8      H          NA 0.00000000   99
###   9      I -0.04768569 0.09722450  100
###   10     J -0.03958305 0.10199014  100

# And this just plain doesn't work, and throws a weird error
cast(test.df2, ctgry ~., c(mean2, sem, len2))

###   Error in `[<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, is.na <http://is.na>(result) & data_col, value = c(NA,  :
###     rhs is the wrong length for indexing by a logical matrix

messages.body_plain:
This doesn't exactly answer your question, but you could use ddply to do the same thing:

library(plyr)
ddply(test.df1, .(ctgry), summarise, mean2 = mean2(value), sem = sem(value), len2 = len2(value))
 # ctgry       mean2        sem len2
 #     A          NA         NA   99
 #     B          NA         NA   99
 #     C          NA         NA   99
 #     D          NA         NA   99
 #     E  0.06946066 0.09761598  100
 #     F          NA         NA   99
 #     G -0.12603771 0.09988778  100
 #     H          NA         NA   99
 #     I -0.04768569 0.09722450  100
 #     J -0.03958305 0.10199014  100

I'd also suggest using reshape2 instead of reshape, but it looks like dcast in reshape2 can only take a single function, not a vector of them.

-Winston
